strengths: Zero console errors and zero page errors across 88 captures (44 routes × desktop and phone).
Every image carries alt text (0 missing on 44 routes), no unnamed buttons or links, no empty hrefs, reduced motion honoured in 62 files, focus states on menus.
No horizontal overflow on any of the 44 routes at 390px. Layouts stack cleanly; the fab model and cycle ring scale.
Six primary sections, three hubs with sub-pages, every page ends in a contact block with 5 to 7 routes to the enquiry. Nothing is more than two clicks from the homepage.
One token set (brand red, square edges, Switzer headings, Instrument Sans body, mono labels) applied on every page; the site reads as one product.
Nothing is invented. Every missing fact is a labelled slot naming the document and who supplies it, so the client knows exactly what to send.
The to-scale timeline (one tick per year) is distinctive and instantly legible: the reader sees the acceleration rather than being told about it.
18 records with market, location, class, area and delivery tags; search, faceted filters, a shortlist that carries into the enquiry form.
Sixteen real roles, filterable by location, department and level, with a plain explanation of how applying works and no invented job descriptions.
Enquiry routed by intent (project, careers, media), the visitor's shortlist attached, eight office cards, a 3D HQ locator.
42 route chunks loaded on demand; React 73K gzipped; a light page is now 1.37MB with three.js deferred until the closing block is near.
Mega menus with a photographic lead panel per wing, a titled Business units column, a skip link, keyboard escape handling, a search that indexes every page and article.
The scroll-built facility is the differentiator the client asked for; it runs on IAQ's own Revit model with a stage rail, zoom controls and a skip.
Twenty real headlines with real dates, a lead-story front page and a plain index, no repetition.
Founding year, years in business, office count and project count now read the same on every page and match IAQ's own discovery answers.
Unknown routes and unknown project ids land on a real 404 with the nav and three ways out.

problems.problem: Every page lives under a hash address (/#/about, /#/services). Search engines index one URL, the homepage. The per-route titles, descriptions and Open Graph tags exist but are never seen by a crawler, a sitemap cannot be written, and shared links preview as the homepage. The client named SEO as a goal on 10 Sep.
problems.evidence: 44 routes all under /#/. Google treats the fragment as one document.
problems.impact: No page other than the homepage can rank; market and service pages, the pages built for search, are invisible to it.
problems.solution: Switch HashRouter to BrowserRouter. Add a host rewrite so every path serves index.html (Netlify _redirects: '/* /index.html 200'; Apache: RewriteRule to index.html; Nginx try_files). Generate sitemap.xml from sitemap.js and reference it in robots.txt. Prerender the 27 static routes at build (vite-plugin-prerender or a puppeteer snapshot step) so crawlers get real HTML. Keep a hash-to-path redirect for old links.
problems.effort: Done in this pass (router, redirect, rewrite files, sitemap); prerender not needed while every route ships meta from the shell
problems.dep: The host applies the rewrite rule before beta; Haydar confirms the platform
problems.status: Done · host must serve the rewrite rule
problems.action: BrowserRouter with base /; hash redirect at boot; _redirects and .htaccess shipped; sitemap.xml on every build; 44 routes re-crawled on real paths.
checks: Crawler: all 44 routes return 200 on clean paths with no #.
Search Console fetch of /about renders the About title and description.
Share /markets/semiconductor on LinkedIn and WhatsApp: preview shows the market title and image.

problems.impact: The pages built for search had the weakest search snippets.
problems.solution: Eight entries added with a description and banner per page.

problems.problem: No skip link; a keyboard user tabbed through the whole menu on every page.
problems.evidence: Nav.jsx.
problems.impact: Slow keyboard navigation; audit finding.
problems.solution: A 'Skip to content' link, visible on focus, that moves focus to the first heading.

problems.problem: Original clips: hero 1.5 to 2.3MB each (four), market clips 1.5 to 2.4MB each (seven), cycle loops 1.1 to 2.4MB each (six). 30MB of video for backgrounds shown under scrims or in 200px panels.
problems.evidence: public/assets sizes before the pass.
problems.impact: Data cost on phones; slow starts; the 3D and hero compete for bandwidth.
problems.solution: Re-encoded to 7MB total (see P02).

problems.problem: The hero strip says Semiconductors, EV Batteries, Data Centres; the band and nav say Semiconductor, EV Battery, Data Centre; the band says Photovoltaic where the route and nav say Photovoltaics.
problems.evidence: Home.jsx hero strip; IndustryGrid.jsx.
problems.impact: Small, but the same market has two names on one screen.
problems.solution: Hero strip uses the market names; band uses Photovoltaics.
problems.action: Strip, band and nav read Semiconductor, EV Battery, Data Centre, Bio LifeScience, Photovoltaics, District Cooling & Heating, Food & Beverage.
checks: Grep: one spelling per market across src.
Hero strip and band read the same names.

problems.problem: 'Member portal' in the public footer and 'Member login' in the phone menu lead to the CMS. A visitor does not know what a member is.
problems.evidence: FooterNav.jsx, Nav.jsx drawer.
problems.impact: Confusing entry point on a public page.
problems.solution: Either label it 'Staff login' and keep it small, or move it to the footer's legal strip.
problems.dep: None; Bazil can rename in FooterNav.jsx and Nav.jsx
problems.action: Every portal entry reads Staff login (nav button label, phone drawer); the public footer columns carry no portal link.
checks: Link present in one place only.

problems.problem: 47 'supplied by IAQ' slots and 31 'concept' notes are visible across the site. Correct for the beta review; none may remain at launch.
problems.evidence: Crawler placeholder counts, 10 Sep.
problems.impact: A public visitor reading a build note.
problems.solution: Every slot is owned above (P25 to P38). The launch build must crawl clean: zero slots, zero notes.
checks: Crawler placeholder count 0 on all routes.
Second crawl on the launch build 24 hours before go-live.
Manual read of the five most-visited pages.

problems.problem: /home2, /about2, /flow and /fab (rejected concepts and the model lab) were live routes.
problems.evidence: main.jsx routes.
problems.impact: Old concepts discoverable by URL after launch.
problems.solution: Not registered in the launch build.

problems.problem: Fourteen prose sentences run 30 to 48 words, several of them the client's copy applied verbatim: the design service lede (42 words), the data centre and photovoltaics market ledes (41, 40), the commitment opener (37), the leadership close (45).
problems.evidence: Crawler text, sentences of 30 or more words.
problems.impact: Long sentences hide the point; on a phone they are a wall.
problems.solution: Rewrite at the copywriting phase after the brand strategy session (14 Sep): one idea per sentence, 20 words or fewer for ledes. Client-verbatim copy is rewritten with Nabilah's sign-off.
checks: No prose sentence over 30 words on the ledes of Services, Markets, About.
Nabilah signs off the rewritten client copy.
Crawler long-sentence count under 3 per page.

problems.problem: Sub-pages (six services, four business unit pages, seven markets, 18 projects) have no breadcrumb; the only way back up is the nav.
problems.evidence: No breadcrumb component in the templates.
problems.impact: A visitor landing from search on a market page has no sense of where it sits.
problems.solution: A one-line breadcrumb (Services › Engineering Design) at the top of the hero on the three page templates, with BreadcrumbList structured data.
problems.action: Crumbs in PageHead with a BreadcrumbList on every sub-page; project pages carry the trail and the data; every item is a real path ending at the page itself.
checks: Breadcrumb visible on a service, a market and a project page.

problems.problem: The hero strip shows four of the seven markets with no way to the other three.
problems.evidence: Home.jsx hero strip.
problems.impact: Three markets are absent from the first screen.
problems.solution: Add 'All seven markets' to the strip, linking to /markets.
problems.action: All seven markets → link at the end of the hero strip, to /markets.
checks: Fits on one row at 1280 and wraps cleanly on phone.

problems.problem: The six value diagrams share one silhouette and do not read apart at a glance (noted by BM on 3 Sep).
problems.evidence: /about values grid.
problems.impact: The section reads as decoration, not six distinct ideas.
problems.solution: Superseded by the ring: each of the six cards carries its own photograph of the value being held on a real site, plus its own line mark, so the six read apart at a glance without six new diagrams.
problems.action: The isometric diagrams came off the page when the ring landed; the six cards now differ by photograph and by mark.
checks: Each reads with its title covered.
